newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks rebound to end above 4,500 points.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks rebound to end above 4,500 points.

text.p: Swiss shares were driven higher on Tuesday by a technical reaction to Monday's losses and the firming U.S. dollar to end back above 4,500 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI).
The outlook was described as positive but the technical situation remained shaky, a dealer said, adding the indices may try to break out of a long-term upward channel in the next few sessions.
The SMI ended at 4,503.9 points, up 40.7 points or 0.91 percent from Monday's close. The day's high was at 4,510.6.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index added 24.52 points to 2,861.52.
Dealers said trade focused on shares with a heavy weighting in the SMI index, such as Novartis, Roche and Nestle.

Novartis registered shares were up 17 francs to 1,776. The stock was sought due to the fact that trade in rights for Ciba Specialty Chemicals, a Novartis unit which will be spun off, starts on Wednesday.
Dealers said that many investors were speculating that Novartis may quickly recover from any possible weakness stemming from the trade in the rights.
In grey market trade, Ciba shares were quoted around 110 francs, valuing the rights at around 100.
Clariant, Nestle, Swissair and Adecco posted big gains. Clariant, which dealers said may be undervalued compared with Ciba Specialty Chemicals, rose 14 francs to 718.
Insurers profited from an upgrade by a U.S. broker, dealers said. Zurich jumped nine francs, or 2.11 percent, to 435.50 francs.
Swiss Re, Elektrowatt and Holderbank were slightly lower.
